In 1970, Page and Plant retired to [Bron-Yr-Aur](/wiki/Bron-Yr-Aur "Bron-Yr-Aur"), a remote cottage in [Wales](/wiki/Wales "Wales"), to commence work on their third album, *[Led Zeppelin III](/wiki/Led_Zeppelin_III "Led Zeppelin III")*.[[44]](#cite_note-48) The result was a more acoustic style that was strongly influenced by [folk](/wiki/Folk_music "Folk music") and [Celtic music](/wiki/Celtic_music "Celtic music"), and showcased the band's versatility. The album's rich acoustic sound initially received mixed reactions, with critics and fans surprised at the turn from the primarily electric arrangements of the first two albums, further fuelling the band's hostility to the musical press.[[45]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWall2008208–209-49) It reached number one in the UK and US charts, but its stay would be the shortest of their first five albums.[[46]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYorke1993130-50) The album's opening track, "[Immigrant Song](/wiki/Immigrant_Song "Immigrant Song")", was released as a US single in November 1970 against the band's wishes, reaching the top twenty on the *Billboard* chart.[[47]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEYorke1993129-51)

Page played his 1959 Dragon Telecaster until a friend stripped Page's custom modifications and repainted the guitar.[[48]](#cite_note-52)[[49]](#cite_note-53) From 1969 onwards the [mahogany](/wiki/Mahogany "Mahogany") "Number 1" Les Paul has been Page's main guitar.[[50]](#cite_note-54)

A **continent** is any of several large terrestrial geographical regions. Continents are generally identified by [convention](/wiki/Convention_(norm) "Convention (norm)") rather than any strict criteria. A continent could be a single large [landmass](/wiki/Landmass "Landmass"), a landmass and nearby islands either on or beyond its [continental shelf](/wiki/Continental_shelf "Continental shelf"), or a part of a larger landmass, as in the case of Asia and Europe within [Eurasia](/wiki/Eurasia "Eurasia"). Due to these varying definitions, the number of continents varies, up to seven or as few as four. Most [English-speaking countries](/wiki/English-speaking_world "English-speaking world") recognize seven continents. In order from largest to smallest in area, these seven are [Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia"), [Africa](/wiki/Africa "Africa"), [North America](/wiki/North_America "North America"), [South America](/wiki/South_America "South America"), [Antarctica](/wiki/Antarctica "Antarctica"), [Europe](/wiki/Europe "Europe"), and [Australia](/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)") (or sometimes [Oceania](/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") or [Australasia](/wiki/Australasia "Australasia")). As Quaker Mill Company, the company was founded in 1877 in Ravenna, Ohio. TThe totals given for *Titanic* at [Box Office Mojo](/wiki/Box_Office_Mojo "Box Office Mojo") and [The Numbers](/wiki/The_Numbers_(website) "The Numbers (website)") are both incorrect. Prior to the 2023 re-release, the totals at both trackers were inflated above the true figure.

* As of 2019, Box Office Mojo correctly recorded that *Titanic* had grossed $1.843 billion on its original release, $344 million from its 3D reissue in 2012, and a further $692,000 from a limited release in 2017 for a lifetime total of $2.187 billion.[[13]](#cite_note-98) Following a limited re-release in 2020, Box Office Mojo incorrectly added $7 million to the original release total.[[14]](#cite_note-99) By the end of 2021, Box Office Mojo had corrected the original release total, but added the $7 million figure to both the 2012 and 2017 reissue totals, incorrectly increasing the lifetime total by $14 million to $2.202 billion.[[15]](#cite_note-100) At the beginning of 2023, Box Office Mojo corrected the total for the 2017 reissue, bringing the lifetime gross down to $2.195 billion, but retained the error in the 2012 reissue.[[16]](#cite_note-101)
* The Numbers does not log individual releases, but had the lifetime total recorded as $2.186 billion in September 2014 (roughly equating to $1.843 billion for the original release and $343.6 million for the 3D reissue).[[17]](#cite_note-102) A couple of weeks later, The Numbers increased the lifetime gross to $2.208 billion, without explanation.[[18]](#cite_note-103)
